id: The Michael Jackson HIStory Show-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Michael Jackson HIStory Show
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Celebrate the creative genius and musical talent of one of the greatest pop singers. The Michael Jackson HIStory Show promises to be a riveting live performance. The full-scale production at the Opera House pays tribute to one of the most significant cultural figures of the 20th century. Expect a stellar live band, choreographed dancers, and authentic costumes. 

Garth Field is at the centre of this performance. He’s often described as electrifying in his role as Michael. Garth is a triple-threat performer with impeccable vocals, dancing, and acting. 

The show tracks Michael’s journey from his early days as a member of the Jackson 5 to his groundbreaking theatrics in the 80s. It goes on to acknowledge his continued domination of pop culture into the 21st century. Hear all the hits like Thriller, Billie Jean, Bad, Beat It, Don’t Stop Til You Get Enough, They Don’t Really Care About Us, and many more.

id: Wellington Phoenix — 2026/27 A-League Mens Season-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Wellington Phoenix — 2026/27 A-League Mens Season
long_description:
Wellington Phoenix FC A-League Men are back in black (and yellow) and fighting proud against the wind. For two decades, New Zealand’s longest-standing professional football club has represented the city across the Tasman. Celebrate this great milestone and be part of another chapter in Phoenix history at six months of home games. 

The season promises plenty of fireworks as the Phoenix rise once more. Schedule highlights include double-headers with the women’s side and a fierce local derby against Auckland FC. Round up your friends and whānau, grab your tickets, and be part of the action as the Wellington Phoenix take the field.

id: The Opera House: After Dark-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Opera House: After Dark
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
This Halloween, step inside The Opera House after hours for an R18 guided experience. Explore the theatre's hidden corners, colourful history, and lingering mysteries. Over the course of an hour, you’ll be led through the building by a guide. They’ll share tales from The Opera House’s past. This includes stories, legends, and strange happenings that have endured long after the final curtain call.   

As you move through the darkness, mysterious figures, unexpected encounters, and eerie effects will keep you wondering what — and who — might be waiting around the next corner. Once you’ve made it back into the light, unwind in the foyer with a complimentary drink and nibbles, included with your ticket.   

Blending theatre history, storytelling, and a touch of Halloween mischief, The Opera House After Dark offers a unique way to experience one of Wellington’s most iconic venues.

Accessibility and safety
You need a good level of mobility to go on this tour. You will be walking through foyers, stairways, and spaces. While there are railings and several rests throughout the tour, you will not have the opportunity to sit for a long period during the tour.   
This tour is currently not accessible for wheelchair users. If you are a wheelchair user, or have other accessibility needs, and would like to attend a tour, please contact us at guestexperience@wellingtonnz.com 
Some sections of the tour will enter seating areas that are steep and may not be suitable for patrons who experience vertigo. 
Closed-toe, flat shoes are required for the tour. No heels or open-toe shoes.

id: Come Together Big End of Year Bash 2026 — Festival Anthems-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Come Together Big End of Year Bash 2026 — Festival Anthems
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Aotearoa’s favourite supergroup returns with their annual end of year celebration. In 2026 the Come Together team are embracing the songs, artists and performances that defined the world’s greatest music festivals. From the revolutionary sounds of Woodstock to the modern stages of Glastonbury and Coachella. Take a journey through the music that's shaped those iconic events.   

The show pays tribute to legendary festival performers including Jimi Hendrix, Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, Queen, U2, The Killers, and more. Come Together’s all-star lineup of New Zealand music talent will take the stage. Jon Toogood, Milan Borich, Jennie Skulander, and Seamus Johnson will be joined by the Come Together band of Jol Mulholland, Brett Adams, Mike Hall, Matthias Jordan, and Alistair Deverick. 

Gather your festival crew, relive some of music’s greatest moments, and close out 2026 with a night of huge anthems, powerhouse performances, and collective nostalgia. The festival spirit is alive and well, minus the rain.

name: Wellington Phoenix — 2026/27 A-League Womens Season
venue: Hnry Stadium and Porirua Park, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Wellington Phoenix FC A-League Women are back in black and fighting proud against the wind. Last season, they made history as the first New Zealand club to reach an A-League Grand Final. Now, the team returns to build on that success and you can cheer them on at six months of home games. 

The season kicks off with a double-header weekend alongside the Phoenix Men at Hnry Stadium. Energy is high as the Phoenix club celebrates 20 years in the capital. On game day, expect plenty of passion, food, and family-friendly entertainment. Bring the whole crew along to watch the team in action, as they continue to raise the bar for women's football in Aotearoa.

id: Shen Yun-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Shen Yun
venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Picture fairies drifting out of clouds and generals charging into battle. Now add tight choreography and a live orchestra. Shen Yun is coming to Wellington’s St James Theatre in February. Bring your kids along to this family-friendly show. It celebrates thousands of years of Chinese culture through classical dance and music. Dreamy scenery and costumes frame every piece. 

The orchestra blends Western symphonic and traditional Chinese instruments. These include the erhu and pipa. You don’t need to swot up about China beforehand. Bilingual emcees introduce each piece, and song lyrics are translated on the backdrop. 

The two-hour show packs in 20 pieces. One moment, you’re experiencing a legend. The next, you’re in a new region or dynasty. Mongolians ride horseback across the grasslands and generals show off their battlefield heroics. You’ll also see the philosophical works of Lao-Tzu and glimpses of heavenly realms. The stories are ancient legends of love, loss, and humour. 

Each year, eight companies, with 500 artists, perform the production across 20 countries. Every season is brand new, from the dances and music to the costumes, stories, and backdrops. Academy Award-winning actor Cate Blanchett called it “exquisitely beautiful”. Come and find out if you agree with her.

id: Game Worlds: Whakaaturanga Pureiapo | Playable Exhibition-Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Game Worlds: Whakaaturanga Pureiapo | Playable Exhibition
venue: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description: It’s more than just the sound of ‘pew pew pew’ that you’ll hear from the national museum on the waterfront. Te Papa hosts ‘Game Worlds: Whakaaturanga Pureiapo | Playable Exhibition’ over summer. The exhibition brings together over 30 of the world’s most influential videogames from the 1970s to today. It invites you to step into extraordinary virtual worlds and discover how videogames are made and how they’ve shaped the way we play and connect.
